title: Ivo and the Orbit
premise: Jonah Marchetti has spent a decade as an insurance investigator of impossible accidents, hiding their past behind paperwork and cargo runs through contested orbits. When the name 'Ivo Marchetti' appears on the manifest of a ship that never flew, Jonah realizes someone is resurrecting a dead identity—Jonah's own—to launder a sabotage plot aimed at the last independent relay in dead space. Pursued by corporate enforcers who want the frame-up buried and haunted by a former partner, Wren, now duty-bound to arrest them, Jonah races to reach the relay before its reactor countdown finishes. In the end, Jonah broadcasts the truth at the cost of their anonymity, chooses Wren over the law that divides them, and lets 'Ivo' die for good so they can finally live under their own name.
about_author: Xanthe Eastwick is the pen name of a former maritime claims adjuster who traded harbor offices for orbital fiction after one too many 'impossible' losses. They write from a converted tugboat moored somewhere off the Atlantic coast, where the shipping lanes still look like star charts.

chapters.title: The Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Processing routine claims, Jonah discovers the name Ivo Marchetti on the manifest of the Calypso Vein—a vessel decommissioned before it ever launched. The impossible paperwork feels like a message. Emotional beat: cold dread beneath professional calm; the past knocking on a door Jonah welded shut.

chapters.title: Paper Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Digging into registry archives, Jonah learns the forged manifest routes insurance payouts to fund something at the Halcyon Relay, the last neutral beacon in dead space. A corporate auditor, Voss, starts asking questions Jonah can't afford to answer. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Wren
chapters.summary: POV alternating Jonah/Wren. Wren Okafor, Jonah's former partner and lover, is assigned to investigate the same fraud—and to bring in whoever wears the name Ivo Marchetti. Their first meeting in ten years is all clipped professionalism over old wounds. Emotional beat: love against duty, both pretending the history isn't there.

chapters.title: Contested Orbit
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Fleeing a staged accident meant to kill 'Ivo' and close the file, Jonah hijacks their own cargo hauler and burns for dead space. Voss's enforcers shadow them; Wren follows on official orders. Emotional beat: grief for the invisible life being jettisoned, thrumming with escape velocity.

chapters.title: Dead Space Radio
chapters.summary: POV Wren. Alone aboard her pursuit cutter, Wren decodes the fraud's true target: not money, but the relay's signal authority—whoever controls it rewrites every contract in contested orbits. She must decide whether justice means the warrant or the truth. Emotional beat: duty cracking under weight.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Running silent through dead space, Jonah finds a stowaway: a relay technician's kid carrying proof of the reactor sabotage. Reactor countdown revealed—forty hours. Emotional beat: reluctant tenderness; protecting someone else forces Jonah to stop running.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Voss boards Jonah's ship mid-flight; Wren arrives in time to tip the fight, officially 'securing the suspect.' The two fugitives and the child barely escape as Voss's ship locks onto their trail. Emotional beat: alliance confessed without words; trust rebuilt in gunfire.

chapters.title: Countdown at Halcyon
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Reaching the dying relay, Jonah crawls into the reactor housing while Wren holds off Voss's boarding party. The saboteur turns out to be the broker who invented 'Ivo'—a ghost-maker selling identities to the highest bidder. Emotional beat: fury transmuted into focus; the clock louder than fear.

chapters.title: Signal Fire
chapters.summary: POV alternating. Climax: Jonah aborts the meltdown and broadcasts the full evidence on the relay's emergency band—burning their own cover forever—while Wren arrests Voss under maritime-adjacent salvage law, justice outside the statute books. Emotional beat: catharsis; visibility chosen, not forced.

chapters.title: Ivo, Resting
chapters.summary: POV Jonah. Weeks later, Jonah files the last claim under their real name, retires the ghost, and signs on as the relay's new keeper. Wren transfers out of enforcement to stay. Emotional beat: quiet resolution—an identity claimed, a love chosen, a light left burning at the edge of dead space.
